messages:
kyle: Hey team — after the VPC migration last night, our app started getting intermittent 500s talking to the internal service endpoint `svc.account.prod.internal`. Traces show TLS handshake failures and the app is resolving the service to a public IP sometimes (weird).

jess: Ugh. Which cluster and which VPC did you move to? Any chance the private hosted zone lost association?

kyle: Cluster: prod-cluster-eu (EKS). VPC: vpc-0a1b2c3d. It used to work then we moved. Quick repro I ran from a pod: 
```
# from inside pod
dig +short svc.account.prod.internal @10.0.2.2
3.12.45.67

curl -v https://svc.account.prod.internal/health
* Rebuilt URL to: https://svc.account.prod.internal/health\n* Trying 3.12.45.67...\n* Connected to 3.12.45.67 (3.12.45.67) port 443 (#0)\n* TLS 1.2 connection using X
* server certificate verification FAILED: certificate is not valid for 'svc.account.prod.internal'\n* Closing connection 0
```
So DNS is returning the public address (3.12.45.67) instead of the private ENI IP. TLS cert mismatch because the public host serves a different cert.

jess: Can you paste `kubectl get pods -n app -o wide` and confirm node-local-dns (nodelocaldns) is still in the new cluster? Also any resolver rules in the account?

kyle: Node local cache is present. We do have a cross-account forwarding resolver rule for `prod.internal` that points to the central resolver IP 10.0.2.2. I checked Route53 quickly and I *think* the private hosted zone for `account.prod.internal` exists, but not sure about VPC associations.

raj: Two common failure modes: 1) Private hosted zone not associated with the new VPC (so the central resolver falls back to public hosted zone), 2) node-local or CoreDNS cache still has the public answer. Also verify resolver rule priority / overlap — if there's a public hosted zone with the same name in another account it can leak answers depending on resolver ordering.

loren: Steps to confirm (AWS CLI):
```
# list associations
aws route53domains list-hosted-zones-by-name --dns-name "account.prod.internal" --query "HostedZones[]" 
# check private hosted zone associations
aws route53 get-hosted-zone --id Z1234567890 --query "VPCs"
# list resolver rules
aws route53resolver list-resolver-rules --filters Name=Name,Values=prod-internal-forward
```

jess: Also check the EKS node-level iptables egress allowlist — sometimes after migrations teams accidentally restrict the egress to central resolvers. If the pods can't reach the private resolver, they'd fall back to internet egress and hit the public host.

kyle: Ran the hosted-zone commands — confirmed there *is* a private hosted zone but it only lists the old VPC (vpc-0f9e8d7c). New VPC (vpc-0a1b2c3d) is NOT associated. No surprise. Looks like nobody associated after the migration.

infra-bot: reminder: runbook link -> https://intranet.redwood/privdns-runbook :page_facing_up:

jess: Okay, that explains the DNS leak to the public IP and the TLS mismatch. Two remediation actions: 1) Associate the private hosted zone with vpc-0a1b2c3d (or create an association change via the infra request flow), 2) Flush node-local cache on the EKS nodes (delete pods to repull or `kubectl exec` to clear nodelocaldns cache)

loren: If you can't immediately associate the hosted zone, a temporary mitigation is to add a resolver rule in the new account pointing `account.prod.internal` to the private resolver IP (if you have permission) — but prefer associating the hosted zone. After association, TTLs might still let the public answer linger; flush caches.

kyle: Associated the hosted zone to vpc-0a1b2c3d and restarted the `nodelocaldns` DaemonSet on the cluster. Re-ran the dig from a pod: 
```
dig +short svc.account.prod.internal @10.0.2.2
10.2.45.11
```
And curl now: 
```
curl -v https://svc.account.prod.internal/health
* Connected to 10.2.45.11 (10.2.45.11) port 443 (#0)\n* TLS 1.2 connection using X
* Server certificate: subject CN=svc.account.prod.internal
* SSL certificate verify ok
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
```
kyle: Service healthy again. Thanks for the pointers. :tada:

jess: Nice job. Leaving notes for postmortem: ensure VPC association checklist in migration runbook, add a quick automated check that the private hosted zone is associated within 30 minutes of any VPC migration.

raj: Also add an automated test that performs a `dig` from a test pod and validates the answer is private-IP for service endpoints. Saves on manual triage time.

kyle: Will open a postmortem ticket and add the runbook change. Thanks all!
